en: Jose Rizal annotated Antonio de Morga's historical book to prove Filipinos already had a rich, independent culture before Spanish colonization.
The Philippine Eagle, our national bird, is one of the largest forest eagles in the world and typically lays only one single egg every two years.
Unlike many other countries, the President of the Philippines is strictly limited to a single six-year term and is absolutely forbidden from running for re-election.
Long before modern video calls, Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the world's first two-way videophone in 1955 using a unique electronic circuit he designed.
The Ifugao built the Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago entirely by hand, carving the mountains without any modern machinery or written blueprints.
Before the Spanish arrived, ancient Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an indigenous writing system where each symbol represents a spoken syllable.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their house exteriors with kiping, which are vibrant, leaf-shaped decorations made entirely from ground rice and food coloring.
Julian Felipe originally composed our national anthem, Lupang Hinirang, as an instrumental march, and the Filipino lyrics were actually added a year later by Jose Palma.
The Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the ancient practice of an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo pioneered a unique Philippine painting technique called backlighting, which uses bright sunlight to highlight the golden tones of rural landscapes.
Marcela Agoncillo, alongside her daughter and a friend, hand-sewed the very first Philippine flag in Hong Kong in just five days before it was unfurled in Kawit.
Vulcan Point is a tiny island located inside a crater lake, which is on Volcano Island, which sits inside Taal Lake, which is on Luzon island.
